result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens is typed to return any and in the shared-mode branch returns a raw fetch Response, while Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data` on the result. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set the Google refresh path reads `token.access_token` on undefined and throws; similarly HubSpot expects a HubspotToken from the SDK in the non-shared branch but a Response in the shared branch. The untyped `any` boundary genuinely conflates incompatible response shapes across branches introduced by this diff.
